Easton Cowan is 21, in his second NHL season, and the Maple Leafs keep handing him more. His ice time over the last ten games is up to 18:37, more than three minutes above where he started, and he has 8 goals and 17 points in 25 games. The Globe and Mail called him part of the silver lining in a dark Toronto season.

The finishing is the part to hold loosely. Eight goals on 5.0 expected goals (the quality of his chances) means he's shooting 16%, up from 12% last season, and that rate rarely lasts. The correction may already be under way: three points in his last ten games, against the 6.7 we'd expect at his minutes.

What should stay is the motor. NHL Edge has him in the 95th percentile for top skating speed and for 20-mph bursts, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season, 94th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists (a small sample, 9 games). The worry, per Evolving-Hockey, was the other end: opponents got more chances with him on the ice in 2025-26.
headline: Easton Cowan's finishing ran hot, then cooled
